context: Animated bar chart race showing World GDP rankings for 15 countries from 1993–2023 with play/pause controls, speed multipliers, and a scrubber.
first_impression: Solid bar chart race with honest zero baseline and proper D3 key functions, but the x-domain recalculates from the visible top-12 subset each frame, causing all bars to visually rescale whenever the leader's GDP changes.
what_works: Zero baseline is correctly enforced (x.domain([0, maxGdp])); all four join selections (bars, labels, flags, values) consistently use d => d.country as the key function, ensuring correct object constancy during rank changes.
what_doesnt: Dynamic domain derived from only the top-12 subset means the x-axis maximum shifts every frame, so a country's bar width encodes its GDP relative to the current leader rather than an absolute scale — bars shrink or grow even when their own value is flat; the 1.08 headroom multiplier compounds this visual instability across time.
